YouTube title seed: That Round Street Cover Has a Job You Missed
YouTube description seed: A correctly sized round cover stays wider than its opening whichever way it turns. Its shape also helps move it. Have you noticed a round cover inside a square frame? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts

Suggested opening hook: This round street cover refuses to fall through.
Suggested opening display: Cover Won’t Fall
Select one meaningful emphasis token from the final opening display copy.

Scene development:
contradiction: close oblique view of the recognizable round cover tilted above its matching frame on a clearly identifiable workshop demonstration prop; it remains supported above the opening. Show the non-passing result without explaining dimensions or showing a square comparison.
clue: higher-angle view as the same prop cover changes orientation but remains outside the opening. A circle and its matching frame stay rigid; do not roll the cover yet.
mechanism: practical top and low side views reveal the seating lip and the cover extending beyond the smaller clear opening. Explain constant width in ordinary words; do not draw a diagram or shrink the disk to manufacture the result.
second_reveal: fact consequence; a gloved hand rolls the same small round prop cover a short distance on its edge along a workbench. Keep it visibly a small prop, not a person casually handling a heavy municipal casting.
payoff: return to a seated round street cover in ordinary pavement; connect the protection against passing through and the ability to roll without introducing new claims.

Source-backed facts:
mechanism: A correctly sized round cover remains wider than its smaller circular clear opening because its width is constant across rotations, so it cannot pass through that opening.
orientation: An ordinary unkeyed circular cover does not need its corners aligned with the frame when it is seated.
consequence: A round cast-iron cover can be moved by rolling it on its edge rather than lifting it for the entire move.

Factual boundaries:
The non-passing claim requires a correctly sized circular cover, an intact matching seat and a clear opening smaller than the cover; it is not a guarantee about damaged frames or mismatched covers.
Not all covers are round. A square outer frame may contain a circular cover; do not confuse the outer frame with the clear opening.
Do not generalize rotation freedom to keyed, hinged, locking or other special covers.
Do not claim that circles are the only possible non-passing shape, and do not claim every square cover falls through its opening.
Do not invent weight, load rating, manufacturer certification or the sole historical reason for using round covers.
Use a visibly small workshop prop for handling and rolling. Do not depict an unprotected person lifting a full-size cover or working over an open live-road hole.
